page: Microsoft Azure D96ls_v7 is a compute-optimized virtual machine belonging to the Dlsv7 server family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 96 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 48 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor operating at 4.2 GHz. The x86_64 architecture includes 480 MB of L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions for accelerated vector and matrix operations. The instance is configured with 192.0 GB of system memory, yielding a resource density of 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. No local storage is bundled with this instance, though it is Premium Storage capable, and it includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark evaluations demonstrate strong multi-core processing capabilities and high-throughput memory performance. The server achieved a top-tier Passmark CPU score of 104,787.21 and a multi-core stress-ng CPU performance score of 95,440.36. Memory bandwidth is highly efficient, reaching 7,017.2 GB/sec for cached small-block reads and 333.72 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads. Cryptographic and compression workloads perform exceptionally well, with single-threaded gzip compression at 36.54 GB/sec and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression at 575.95 GB/sec. Additionally, the processor's matrix extensions assist in medium-model prompt processing, reaching 304.72 tokens per second.

From a resource allocation perspective, the D96ls_v7 offers high compute density but presents a clear tradeoff in memory capacity, providing only 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. This makes it highly cost-efficient for CPU-bound workloads that do not require massive in-memory datasets. The lack of bundled local storage requires external storage attachment, which should be factored into architectural planning. This server is highly suited for compute-intensive tasks such as software compilation, ray tracing, high-throughput web serving, and medium-scale machine learning inference.
